carousels.name: Two weeks without p*rn: what changed

slides.title: Two weeks without p*rn. [[Here's what people say changed.]]
slides.sub: If you made it this far — read this. If you didn't — read it twice.

slides.title: The [[itch]]
slides.body: Constant thoughts about p*rn. Restless evenings. "Is it really this hard?" Yes. And it passes.

slides.title: The [[wave]]
slides.body: Many people describe the strongest p*rn urges here — plus irritability and bad sleep. Many people say this is where their NNN ended.

slides.title: The [[boredom]]
slides.body: Fewer spikes, more emptiness. Evenings feel long without p*rn. This is where new habits get built.

slides.title: The first [[clarity]]
slides.body: Many describe small wins: better mornings, less guilt, catching urges earlier. Everyone's different — but two weeks is real proof you can do it.

carousels.name: Saturday is NNN's most dangerous day

slides.title: No work. No plans. Phone in hand. [[Today is p*rn's favorite day.]]
slides.sub: Plan your Saturday — or p*rn will plan it for you.

slides.title: The [[lie-in]] trap
slides.body: Waking late, scrolling in bed, nowhere to be. Many people say their Saturday p*rn relapses start before they get up.

slides.title: The [[3 PM]] slump
slides.body: Bored, alone, nothing on. The afternoon is wide open — for p*rn.

slides.title: The [[late]] night
slides.body: No alarm tomorrow, so you stay up. Tired + alone + late = the classic p*rn setup.

slides.title: Your Saturday [[plan]]
items: Up before 9 — out of bed, phone down.
One plan with people in the afternoon or evening.
slides.note: Save this and use it every Saturday until December 🔖

carousels.name: 8 signs your brain is healing from p*rn

slides.kicker: Save this for a hard day
slides.title: 8 signs you're [[healing from p*rn addiction]] — even if it doesn't feel like it.
slides.sub: Recovery is quiet. Look for these.

slides.title: Signs [[1–4]]
items: Urges feel weaker or shorter than before.
You can sit with boredom without reaching for p*rn.
You feel emotions you used to numb.

slides.title: Signs [[5–8]]
items: You've stopped lying about your p*rn use.
You're thinking about who you want to be.

slides.title: Healing isn't [[loud]].
slides.body: No single day where everything clicks. Just a slow shift away from p*rn. Count the quiet signs.

slides.title: Seeing [[3 or more]]?
slides.body: Then quitting p*rn is working — even if the urges still show up. Keep going. This is what progress looks like.
slides.note: How many signs do you see? Send this to someone who thinks they're not improving ↗

carousels.name: You're not too busy to quit p*rn

slides.title: "I'm too busy to work on it." [[You found time for p*rn every night.]]
The time you [[already have]]
slides.body: 30 minutes of p*rn a day is about 182 hours a year. You don't need extra time to quit. You need to take that time back.

slides.title: Busy is a [[shield]]
slides.body: "After this deadline." "When things calm down." Meanwhile, p*rn never misses a night.

slides.title: Quitting takes [[minutes]]
slides.body: Blocking p*rn: 2 minutes. Phone out of the bedroom: 10 seconds. Telling a friend: one text. No calendar needed.

slides.title: Do it [[now]]
items: Move your charger out of the bedroom.

slides.title: 1 in 10 men struggle to control sexual urges. [[Almost none of them talk about it.]]
slides.sub: The silence around p*rn addiction, in numbers.

slides.title: Of [[men]]
slides.body: A JAMA Network Open study (2018) found 10.3% of men and 7% of women reported real distress from trouble controlling sexual urges and behavior — p*rn use often included.

slides.title: Ever [[get help]]
slides.body: The International Sex Survey (Bőthe et al., 2024) found only 4–10% of people with problematic p*rn use had ever sought treatment.

slides.title: Why the [[gap]]?
slides.body: Shame. Jokes. "Everyone watches p*rn." Not knowing help exists. Millions struggle. Few speak.

slides.title: Close the [[gap]]
items: Find support — a group, an app, a professional.
